findings.title: OS-TRB-ADV-00 [High]: Locker Whitelist Bypass
findings.description: The locked-voter program implements a privileged locking mechanism via the ApproveProgramLockPrivilege instruction, which is intended to restrict token locking to whitelisted programs and escrow owners. However, the instruction fails to validate that the provided governor account matches the governor associated with the locker. This missing check allows an attacker to use a fake governor account to create a whitelist entry for any locker. As a result, the whitelist mechanism can be bypassed entirely, enabling unauthorized programs or users to lock tokens in privileged lockers. The impact of this vulnerability is significant, as it undermines the access control model of the system, potentially allowing malicious actors to manipulate voting power or gain unauthorized privileges within governance processes.

findings.title: OS-TRB-ADV-01 [High]: Insufficient checks for lock privileges revoking
findings.description: The RevokeProgramLockPrivilege instruction allows any party to revoke program lock privileges for a locker without verifying that the provided governor account matches the actual governor of the locker. The validation logic only checks that the smart wallet signer matches the governor's smart wallet and that the whitelist entry is associated with the locker, but it omits a critical check: whether the provided governor account is the legitimate governor of the locker. This flaw enables an attacker to use a fake governor account to revoke legitimate whitelist entries, leading to potential denial of service or unauthorized modification of locker permissions. The impact includes disruption of expected governance operations and potential loss of control over privileged locking mechanisms.
